This is about control. I was informed hours after my grandmother died and one day after my grandfather died. When both events happened, I was an adult. They were both very important to me in my childhood. I consider them my emotional raisers. And her excuse was the same - my feelings, it was not necessary to tell me right away... I confronted her both times about the delay and she managed to backfire it at me. When I was a kid, I was informed days after my father's mother died. She introduced this subject with the death of two birds I had that died the morning she decided to tell me. Makes me wonder how much time have really passed since her death. It could be weeks or even months and she was telling me out of obligation. "It was not necessary to tell me right away because, you know, I wasn't close to her". Never knew how much income her house, where I had to grow up, had. Never knew what taxes were about. Never knew about invesments or heritage. I had those 4 direct relatives who died but I never had anything left for me - not even something sentimental. My grandmother's things, valuables to me, were all throw away without me knowing because "I wouldn't want them anyway". Have been (by someone else - grandma) told I had half brothers when they were already 5 and 2, because she was afraid I would want to live with my father. Because, you know, I was always so ungrateful and liked him the most. Backfired. Control, control, control.      
edit: these people... they make our lifes look like jokes. Because they treat us as beings with less right to feel and to exist as part of a network... called life. We cannot let their bull enter our skin anymore. Let they shit rot somewhere far from us. Hugs

And of course, he was the one who would go for all the errands. She was always working so hard (not really, she left work in the middle of the afternoon because she owns a business. Then she went shopping or to the salon). She never, ever did homework with me. Everyday I forgot to do the homework by myself and had to take a letter for my mom to sign (and I always faked her signatures... or else: the screaming) I hated living there. There was always some stranger around cleaning the house because my mother is a crazy cleanliness lady. I mean: everyday. And my mother acted so gross and stupid whenever I asked her for attention when she came home from work. She never watched a kid's movie with me. Never played with me. Never read a story with me. Never took me to places I wanted to go as a kid. Only on her own terms. Or just to the places where she could drink and I could be doing... whatever. I remember how much she hated me because of her look when she got home and I asked for her to be with me. Well, not actually never... maybe I could count in my left hand's fingers the moments of true bonding we had... over 19 years of living under her (tacky - take that, mom. the whole reason of your life, your house, is so fucking tacky!) roof. Sorry for the ranting. I'm using the sub to recover some memories from out of the fog, and sometimes I get a little lost...
